news_drafts.headline: Carmarthenshire forecasts £11.3m net overspend for 2026/27 after £1,755k overspend in 2025/26
news_drafts.lead:
Carmarthenshire County Council forecasts an overspend of £11.3m on its net revenue budget for 2026/27, against £15.9m at departmental level including schools, according to the budget monitoring report to its Corporate Performance and Resources Scrutiny Committee. For 2025/26 the net position was an overspend of £1,755k, which the paper says has been transferred from general balances.

The report says forecast departmental overspends are met from departmental reserves where available, in line with existing policies, and gives no reserve balances. Children's Services ended 2025/26 with a £3.6m overspend, £0.6m better than the previous reporting period, and forecasts a further £5.4m overspend this year after £12m of pressures funding allocated in previous years. The paper attributes this mainly to growth in children in very high-cost residential placements, with more than 10 new placements since January 2026, partly offset by children turning 18 and moving to Adult Services. Welsh Government's employers' National Insurance grant came in just below £6.0m against a £7.0m budget assumption; the £1.0m shortfall is validated into the 2026/27 final budget.

Schools delegated budgets overspent by £7.7m in 2025/26, met by a matching transfer from school balances, and balances stood at a £9,561k deficit at 31 March 2026. Schools forecast a £6.9m overspend against in-year budgets this year, which the paper acknowledges as an improvement on the previous year. It calls the trajectory "unsustainable" and says an intervention board will provide additional support.

news_drafts.headline: Carmarthenshire's Council Fund overspend reaches £1.76m, covered by reserve draw
news_drafts.lead: Carmarthenshire Council spent £1.755m more than its original budget in the year to 31 March 2026, and covered the shortfall by drawing from its general reserves. The Council Fund — the main account for day-to-day running costs — finished the year with General Balances of £15.497m. The council's Governance & Audit Committee received the outturn figures on 28 September. The overspend required a transfer from the reserve cushion the council holds for unexpected costs. Councils must hold sufficient reserves to manage in-year pressures and to smooth funding across years; the remaining balance provides the buffer for future risk.

news_drafts.headline: Dyfed Pension Fund cleared by auditors as investment income falls short by £6m
news_drafts.lead: Audit Wales has completed its 2025–26 audit of the Dyfed Pension Fund with no issues raised, giving the fund a clean financial bill of health. However, the fund is forecast to end the year £2.9m in deficit, driven chiefly by investment income falling £6m short of the amount budgeted. The fund was counting on that income to balance its books after employer contributions were cut following the 2025 actuarial valuation. The shortfall reflects lower distributions from fund managers and interest on cash holdings than anticipated. The fund has responded by building cash reserves to £18.5m — higher than historically held — described as a prudent measure given the structural changes to contributions.

findings.headline: Fencing works at CSTLC have been paused, with the paper citing cost increases and funding options being considered.
findings.detail: The Additional Learning Needs (ALN + ASD) Projects line is forecast at £1,298k against a £1,743k working budget, a variance of -£445k. The paper says options for funding are being considered.
findings.matters: Pausing a scheme because of cost increases, with the funding route still open, is a pressure other councils running similar school projects could recognise.
findings.quote: Fencing works at CSTLC paused because of cost increases.

findings.headline: Sustainable Communities for Learning - Match Funding Delivery Fund is forecast at £0 against a £44,805k working budget, with the paper saying the funds will be used for future schools projects.
findings.detail: The variance is -£17,849k. The paper records that the budget is to be utilised for future schools projects rather than in 2026/27.
findings.matters: A large education match-funding pot being held for future projects is the single biggest single-line movement in the programme and shows how the council's schools investment is being re-phased.
findings.quote: To be utilised for future schools projects.

findings.headline: Local Regeneration Fund - 8-14 Vaughan Street is forecast at £2,005k against a £6,743k working budget, with the paper saying the Llanelli market will be completed in future years.
findings.detail: The variance is -£4,246k. The paper gives no reason beyond the project completing in future years.
findings.matters: A large regeneration scheme moving out of the current year reduces the budget that must be funded now, and grant-funded schemes of this kind affect the timing of external income.
findings.quote: Project will deliver a new Market for Llanelli which will be completed in future years.

findings.headline: Plas y Bryn's start date has moved to October 2026, which the paper attributes to planning issues including marine nitrates.
findings.detail: Care Home Schemes are forecast at £1,329k against a £19,710k working budget, with a variance of -£5,529k. The paper says future monitoring will reflect the new delivery profile.
findings.matters: Nutrient rules affecting planning in some parts of Wales are delaying social care capital projects, which other councils in similar areas could face.
findings.figures: Care Home Schemes working expenditure £19,710k; forecast £1,329k; variance -£5,529k
findings.quote: Plas y Bryn start date delayed until Oct'26 because of planning issues

findings.headline: Levelling Up Carmarthen West & Pembs South (LUF029) is forecast at £9,309k against a £5,373k working budget, and the paper records that its funding is still to be identified.
findings.detail: The variance is £435k. The paper does not state the source of the additional funding in this appendix.
findings.matters: A forecast cost increase on a grant-funded scheme with no identified funding is an exposure a finance director must close, and lenders look at how such gaps are covered.
